title: Technology Sector Update for 07/05/2018: MU,AMSC,QRVO,INFY

Tech stocks are rebounding strongly in Thursday trading, with shares of technology companies in the S&P 500 index rising more than 1.2% while the Philadelphia Semiconductor index was ahead by more than 2.4% in afternoon trading.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Micron Technology ( MU ) was almost 2% higher Thursday afternoon, retracing a portion of its 3.5% gain soon after the opening bell, that followed the memory chipmaker saying its subsidiaries in China were hit with a preliminary injunction from a Chinese regional court barring them from manufacturing, selling or importing certain Crucial and Ballistix-branded DRAM modules and solid state drives in China. Two rivals - United Microelectronics Corp and Fujian Jinhua Integrated Circuit Co - had sought the injunction after previously filing suit against Micron in retaliation for Micron suing the companies in federal court in the United States alleging misappropriation of Micron trade secrets and after Taiwanese authorities indicted UMC and three of its employees on similar charges. Micron estimates the preliminary injunction likely will trim its Q4 revenue by about 1% although it reiterated its current guidance expecting between $8.0 billion to $8.4 billion in revenue. Analysts, on average, are looking for Micron Tech to generate about $8.25 billion in Q4 revenue.
In other sector news:
+ Qorvo ( QRVO ) was trading higher Thursday afternoon, climbing over 5%, after analysts at Keybanc raised their investment rating for the specialty chipmaker to Overweight from Sector Weight.
- Infosys ( INFY ) retreated Thursday, sinking nearly 2%, despite the technology outsourcing company saying it is partnering with Siemens PLM Software to develop applications and services for the Siemens unit's MindSphere operating system. Under terms of the companies' collaboration agreement, Infosys will provide end-to-end implementation services and post-implementation support for the open cloud-based internet-of-things operating system connecting machinery and other equipment to the digital world.
- American Superconductor ( AMSC ) was falling hard on Thursday, dropping over 16% in recent trading, after the specialty chipmaker late Tuesday announced a settlement with Sinovel Wind Group Co Ltd resolving all of their existing commercial disputes. The settlement calls on the Chinese wind turbine manufacturer to pay $57.5 million to American Superconductor through two installments, with the first payment due Thursday and the second installment due in about 10 months, in return for American Superconductor providing Sinovel with a non-exclusive license to some of its intellectual property and to be used solely with Sinovel's doubly fed wind turbines. The license agreement will terminate if Sinovel fails to make the second payment.
